We completed the entire trail as noted on this app. We started early on a Thursday at 7:15 am with prepaid parking. The parking lot was empty and portable bathrooms are available only in the parking lot. We finished the trail in 8 hours, stopping for lunch and snacks and at just about every look out along the escarpment. 

The entire trail is very well marked and groomed. The entire hike is not recommended for a novice hiker as there are a lot of tree roots and rocks to maneuver around and in many areas along the escarpment there are many areas where you are climbing up or down and it’s hard even with a walking stick.

Even if you are only walking to the Lions Head outlook you need proper hiking shoes.
All the outlooks require climbing onto boulders where one slip could mean falling off the cliffs.

The hike was fantastic and we will do it again.  There was a lot of mosquitoes along the bush section of the track so bring along bug spray.

Difficult trail.  Lots of elevation changes. 

Views and look out points were among the best on the Bruce.

gorg lake views from the cliffs. the way back through the forest is much lighter. only really crowded for the first few km to the lookout, most people dont do the full loop. we did a quick dunk in the water at the rocky beach that the trail goes through, cold but shallow. overflow parking is paid and a couple km from the trailhead.
Good trail for Ontario, some of the terrain was on the harder side of moderate but overall quite nice with good views.
Hard. Very hard. Hiking boots and poles are recommended.
got going 8am so only saw 2 people all day!  beautiful and well marked trail
so so beautiful, i love outside
Book parking in advance
Parked at cemetery road. Had water, poles, snacks, rain coat, wasn’t over dresses. Rain a bit. Put my foot in the water. The section after look out was not busy. Little bugs, little mud.
It’s rockier than you’d expect… and lots of “am i going the right way”

Absolutely beautiful loop!  Bring snacks and water taking in all the views will extend the time youre on trail.  Hiked mid April, still technically off season so no reservation or parking fee needed.  First 1/3 very well marked blazes closely spaced, remainder has sections that have much bigger gaps between markers.  Keep your eyes open.  Trail is well maintained, but in such a big network you will run into downed trees.  Waterproof footwear for spring hikes isn't essential but highly recommended

This trail was very tough for the first half. Lots of rock climbing etc. I had a couple difficult spots where I needed to assist the dogs. The second half was through the forest, which was an easy end to the day.
Best off season hiking. I completed 16 km in 3 hours.

The trailhead to the lookout was super crowded but continuing on after the lookout and I didn’t see a single person. Plenty of viewpoints along the path, which is well marked. The terrain is moderate to difficult; not much incline but very rocky in many places. Not too much scrambling though.

Definitely a challenge. Started at the McCurdy parking lot and took the Bruce all of the way to lookout #5 (as called out on this map) The more you hike, the more difficult it becomes. Amazing views, as long as you can stomach hiking escarpment edge. I did take the inland trail back to the main trail and it was a great change from the climbing. Total of 16k.
It was definitely hard and it’s easy to get lost. The views are beautiful.
The trail is not very hard, but you definitely need to wear hiking shoes. It was quite busy at the beginning and well-marked along the way.
Fairly typical Bruce Trail composition - rocks and roots aplenty. Views of the gorgeous Georgian Bay separate this portion from the interior. Sturdy shoes recommended to avoid ankle rollapalooza.

Stunning. Dozens of gorgeous overlooks as you walk along the escarpment, plus a lovely section walking along the shoreline. Don’t miss the little detour that will give you about 400 meters along the shore. You could extend it by walking all the way to/from McKay bay if the waterline is low like it is in 2025. 

We did it in reverse taking the advice of others here who said to park free on Cemetery Road. Rocks can be slippery, so do plan more time than your usual hike. This took us seven hours! But we went slow and picnicked in a couple of places.
A tough trail even in good weather conditions. Much slower going than other sections of the Bruce Trail. Feels good to have completed this.

As a casual/intermediate hiker, I have not found this trail to be challenging - I would say intermediate. The conditions were easy, a little technical but definitely not difficult. The length made it an intermediate hike. The views are amazing all along the trail. The lookout is the most impressive but there are many stunning views all along as you follow along the ridge. Walking poles recommended. Bring enough water and food. It took us 6h16 minutes (stopping for plenty of photos and snack breaks) for a total of 18 KM. I definitely recommend this hike ! Do make sure to go early though to avoid the crowds and you have to reserve the parking in advance, especially for the full day parking pass which you will definitely need.
mostly a slog, main viewpoint had about 30 people on it yelling and doing photoshoots. very quiet on the rest of the trail, none of the rest of the viewpoints are as good as the main one

Beautiful trail. Hot day and the humidity was a killer, but three route itself was stunning. Some great views. Ok maintenance, the white trail markers are an interesting choice but you will definitely be able to follow along. The trail is moderately quiet in the beginning, but gets very busy closer to the lookout point until you hit the trail back to parking lot B. Runs close to cottages and roads at times, as is characteristic of the Bruce Trail. I prefer this park over the peninsula, much quieter although still busy.

Amazing trail if you want a long hike! Some of the trail was a bit overgrown but overall great. Quite incredible views, does get crowded around lions head tho. We did 15.63km, which includes the whole long trail. Free parking too at cemetery road too! Wouldn’t bring kids or pets on the full long hike as it gets a bit dangerous at points

We started the loop trail at the Cemetery Rd parking which was free. There is a paid lot at the other end of the loop closer to Lions Head Town center. When we arrived at the lot at the end of our loop there there was a fee to park but they did have a free shuttle service on Sat at least (could have been Friday and Sunday as well) that took us to the beach area where we were able to fill our water bottles because by the end of the 15km we were out of water lol overall the trail had so many awesome views points, because we started on the opposite end to the majority of the crowds, we hiked for the first 3hr without passing or seeing any people. The trail was single file for a great deal of that portion as well. Poles may be helpful.
Weekdays are the best to avoid crowds., if you start out at 6am ...

Stunning views all around! Parking requires reservations beforehand. Can get really crowded on weekends up until the main lookout, but mostly clears up afterwards. Last stretch of the hike has a lot of overgrowth and some poison ivy to watch out for!

Limited parking availability during peak season from may to September at the trail entrance, so book in advance, else, have to park near the beach or school or find any near by public parking. 
Hike is bit challenging but manageable.
Long hike get the full day pass or park the the school nearby to avoid a ticket.

One of the best trails in Ontario. The scenery is absolutely stunning with views of the turquoise waters and beautiful forest.  The full loop takes around 6 hours ( more, if you spend time on the rocky beaches midway through the loop) , so plan to start early.
Avoid it doing in Wet conditions but good weather it is worth to complete the loop of the trail.

Beautiful trail. Parked at the end of cemetery road and did the trail counter clockwise. We did the full 16.6km loop in 4hr 22mins. The first 12km were lovely with very little traffic. The last 4km before splitting off on a side trail to return to our car was crowded with large groups of people with very poor hiking etiquette. Please remember to move over and let faster hikers pass you! 
The trail is challenging with footing. A lot of rocks and roots to navigate. Not too much change in elevation overall. There were a few short sections of climbing but nothing too challenging. Awesome vistas and look outs along the cliffs. Appropriate hiking footwear is a must. 
Today’s weather was perfect. A little cool, a nice breeze so no bugs and very comfortable temperatures. 
Overall, a beautiful hike that was challenging but not overwhelming.
Absolutely incredible! Challenging, engaging hike with spectacular views.
not the best when its raining, took forever because it was so slippery! however, very rewarding to finish and the sights were worth it
Perfect day for it..  no debris, no bugs (yet)
Lots fallen trees directly on the trail. Many times difficult to pass. It must of happened like 2 days ago or so. But the views were worth it.
long!!!! but epic

5 .5 hours to do this trail is NOT accurate! Add atleast 2 hours or more. It’s a beautiful trail with stunning views but you need to watch your footing . Once we got past  the “Look outs” that most people go to, turn around and go back we continued on to complete the loop and we saw no one. We ended up taking the road to get back to the parking lot bc it was more than we anticipated. Just be prepared for a longer hike than this app suggests. The trail is stunning but it is difficult with a lot of it being on a cliff edge. Totally fantastic day but just be prepared.
Great views, climbing involved in several parts but totally worth it. Bring enough water.

The first half on the east side is quite tough and a little bit slippy. Once you hit Lion's Point the trail becomes very easy. I opted to take the full Bruce trail around the peninsula instead of cutting inland which was longer. You also get to stop at the beach that way. Didn't see a single person during the first half. Great escape

Gorgeous trail, gorgeous lookout. The trail is very rugged; lots of slippery rock and roots. Good hiking boots are a MUST. I was shocked by the number of folks on this trail with basic runners on. I also recommend hiking early morning as it gets super busy around 10am. You just register for parking online; 4hr parking is $20, I think whole day is $30. 10/10 will be back to this trail again.
There was a bit of mud. Wear proper hiking clothing and boots as there is a lot of up and down. You will get a bit of everything on this hike!
This hike always fills the soul. Pack some food, make a day of it. We had the lookout all to ourselves at sunset. Beautiful! Little spots of mud but no biting insects.
Very rocky and a few off trails that lead to nowhere, had to find our way back on the trail a few times but the views were amazing

Thank you for tips on parking   .  We parked at the very end of cemetery road and did the loop counter clockwise.  It was not crowded and there were some beautiful places to swim. It was buggy so be prepared and wear trail shoes.

This trail clocks in about 19-20km, which feels like quite a lot when you read from AllTrails that it's just over 16km. 

We parked at the school in Lion's Head and walked about 800 metres to the trailhead. This is because parking is expensive and typically full at the trailhead. Once you're on the trail, you'll go for a bit and arrive at a junction - if you go left, you will start with the Lion's Head lookout (very crowded) or continue straight (counter-clockwise on the loop). That's what we did. And to be honest, we chatted most of the hike about that decision, was it best to go straight or should we have followed the lookout path first? 

Please note, the POISON IVY is no joke along the trail for about 10km.  You cannot avoid it, it drips on the trails, it breezes onto the trail, and it lives on the trail. Wear tall socks, or long pants - or just be totally cool with getting poison ivy. 

There are so many lookouts, and gorgeous areas for the first 10km (*again if you start the opposite from the lookout). But once you start to creep closer to the lookout (7km out) , the crowds begin to thicken. And the views become less appealing because of the crowds. We estimated we passed close to 100 people the final 7km.

I don't know. I'm still recovering and feeling totally spent. Just don't go in the rain. Do you know what happened to us? We got caught in the rain. Even though it was supposed to be sunny. Sometimes that's happens. But for the love of god, wear hiking boots. It was PROFOUND to witness those in flip-flops, 'fashion sneakers', and horrifying footwear. This trail is technical. And kinda wild at times, like really, really wild. Wear hiking boots / or hiking shoes.

Anyway,

You know what, scroll down and read Michael L's review. He seems to know what he's doing.
It’s a long and challenging trail. Bring lots of water and snacks. Proper hiking boots are a must as the trail is quite rugged after the lookout section.

The trails were definitely not for the faint of heart, lots of ups and downs, long runs, and pretty much climbing up and down rocks every 200m. Trails are NOT maintained. Maybe the first 2km in but everything after that is overgrown and some paths don’t look like they are the paths for walkers. If you go, be aware of all the surrounding while walking.
Most people only make it to the lookout, after that you see less and less. Didn’t see anyone after 5.3km
We did the hike in the rain well most of it. So muddy and slippery but way too many people doing the 7 km lookout were not wearing proper foot gear.

Exceptional high point on the edges with breathtaking view to the Georgian Bay. The crystal clear and deep blue colour of the water felt like illusion! It is the best to start from the parking lot from Cemetery Rd and go counter clockwise.  We went on a windy day in 19 C, not a lot of sunshine but that whats I always dream of! The Breeze in the Jungle was way far from any AC. Bugs & mosquito activities was low despite there was a rain in the night before
Mostly a walk through forest- typical of Bruce trail. Great lookout point - although quite busy. My favourite was the pebbly beach just past the lookout.
A must do if in the area. Some of the most spectacular views of barrow bay and lion’s head.
Lots of up and down. Good hiking shoes required!
difficult to walk must bring trek pole
Plan for a long hike with many conditions.
Great trail overall. Lots of rocks on trail. Great leg workout.

Great trail, challenging enough to make it interesting. Well maintained and marked. Almost no bugs at all. The only part with some foot traffic is by the Lion’s Head Lookout Point. The remaining 15 km saw two people.

Check out Step it Up Adventures full trail review for a 4 day hike from Tobermory to Barrows Bay.   Click on this link or search www.stepitupadventures.ca. 
Blog, Explore and Learn about Outdoor Adventure, Step it Up Adventures https://share.google/kcfbiJZqvHK5D3H5p
Good hiking boots

Considerably tougher than expected hike. Super rewarding to find something like this in Ontario. Lots of up and down sections not reflected on the elevation. Wear good hikers. A few ankle twisting/ foot sliding in shoes sections even for advanced hikers. Some sections were excellent to run. Some sections are very rough terrain. 
Such a beautiful spot!
WARNING: significant Poison Ivy on trail from Cemetery Rd parking lot to Lookout

Date hiked: Fri May 31 ///// Time taken: 5.5h including some short breaks, going counterclockwise, we also added the Warder side trail which made it almost 18km total ///// Beauty: 6.5/10 ///// Difficulty: 6.5/10 due to frequently challenging terrain ///// Cautions: occasional cliff edges but mostly optional, should be fine for experienced kid hikers over maybe age 10 ///// How easy to follow trail: helpful blazes on trees to guide the way, but still occasionally a bit challenging ///// People encountered: 7 people over the first 13km then 60 over the last 5km ///// Shade: 80-90% shade ///// Wildlife: butterflies, one small garter snake,  Weather: sunny, 13-17°C so basically perfect ///// Varying ecosystems/terrains: mostly forest floor with frequent roots and rocks, lots of ups and downs, one short rocky beach section ///// Overgrowth: mild to moderate, especially the Eastern 1/3 of the hike ///// Bugs: minimal mosquito density, no bug spray used and only got one or two bites ///// Summary: nice challenging hike consisting of mostly beautiful forest hiking, with frequent lookouts over the bay and one rocky beach that makes a nice rest stop around 70% or the way through the when going counterclockwise. Also some shortcut trail options when going this way, which is the reason we chose this direction, but didn’t end up needing them. Reserve a spot at the McCurdy lot early

I loved it. I started at the end of Cemetery Rd and went clockwise. Beautiful trek through the forest and great views from the cliffs. This trail was interesting because it felt like it was constantly shifting terrain. Flat forest sections, rock ledges, hills with different grades, bright green areas, and dark forest sections. It felt very long but nearly the entire trail is shaded. Trail is very well marked.

The only danger was the cliffs. If you don’t act stupid near the cliff edges you should be fine. I am glad I did this one without the kids because the length would have been too much for them.

https://youtube.com/shorts/n8Mh1T8-y5Q
saw lots of blue jays and chipmunks. also found a snake by the beach. lots of ups and downs along the trail, quite the hike.
Very Rocky and difficult and spots. Beautiful nonetheless. I highly recommend coming here
it was wet and slippery in the middle of the trail
Extremely rocky, so bring appropriate footwear! Everything is worth it, the views, the beach, it’s all spectacular.
It was a bit slippery on rocks. Great and challenging trail for any hiking enthusiast. Give yourself a 6-8 hours depending on speed and weather conditions.

We went the morning after it rained all night. Rocks were slippery and the path was sludgy. Once the sun comes out, the rocks dry up rather quickly and grip comes easy. 
Carry Lots of water, solid shoes with good grip, carry snacks for fuel along the way. We did the full loop, took 6.5 hours of hiking at a comfortable 3km/hr. Have fun!
Took us a solid 5 hours and 30 mins. Beautiful views along the way
Hard train
Took 5 hours at a high pace. Lots of steep rocks with large steps.

Such a fun hike!! Distance is defs longer than it states. For me it was 18km. After reading other reviews I anticipated it’d be longer than what was stated! Really fun climbs and beautiful viewpoints throughout the entire trail! Worth the trip for sure!
Lots of up and down for the first half, last half was nice and smooth. Bring a decent amount of water and good footwear. Full of beautiful views. We stopped at the bay for a nice long swim and lunch.

A beautiful hike! It took us just under 5 hours at a moderate pace and found the trail to not be too challenging . One thing to note like others have mentioned is that the hike is longer than the 15.9km stated.
I'm tired. My legs hurt.
It’s so lonnggggggg
Great trail. Would recommend leaving yourself at least 6 hours so that you can enjoy the lookout points

A long, but rewarding hike. We calculated the loop to be closer to 17.5 km, and took us about 6h 45 min to complete. Not many bugs at all. Going clockwise, we found the best views to be on the first half / left side of the loop.

Great trail! Definitely need good shoes for the full loop. It gets tough near the lookout and then around the rest of the trail until you get back in the forest. I went super early to beat the crowd and it was quiet.
Amazing view
Convenient shuttle service.
Best hike in Ontario, but not for the faint of heart
Best trail I’ve ever been on.  Very challenging not many bugs and the views are out of this world.  World class.  Marked very well too.
Best view in Bruce Trail. Worth driving seven hours out and back for the trip.
amazing hike and day!!

Not many bugs
Lots of elevation changes
Rock terrain was very slippery when wet
Busy for the lookout area hike but nice for the rest
Only one access to water. Use it wisely.

Nice trail even on an overcast day. ( also had some of the smoke from the wildfires). Trail marked well in majority of spots. The odd time we had to stop and check thqt we were folloqing the proper path and not the ones made by other people.  This trail ia marked as 16km. My sister and I were both wearing our Fitbits and both got closer to 20 km. Give yourself about 4 1/2  to over 5 hours for this one.
Nice trail. Not busy after the first lookout even on Canada Day weekend. Bring your garbage out with you. I picked up so many cans and bottles. Disgusting
Incredible views, strenuous but well maintained and marked trails.  Very few mosquitoes!  The eastern part of the loop is very tranquil, past just a few people that half.
Very clean, easy to navigate. Full 17 km is advanced & if you don’t want to complete the whole loop, I would suggest the lookout then hike to the rock beach. Amazing!

Fanatic trail. This trail took us 8.5 hours. We could have done it in 7.5 but we had a few blips along the way. Definitely pre-stray with bug stray and reply half way. Views are spectacular. Highly recommend this hike.

Great picturesque trail 
Well marked
Good quality Ontario hike. Great views. Trail slightly technical with all the rocks so it keeps your mind engaged.
My first hike ever. This kicked my butt but felt very rewarding when finished. Bring lots of snacks and water and make sure you keep an eye out on the sun. Barely made it out before sunset.
Beautiful views once the fog cleared. Worth taking the inland trails which have a ton of trillium and other wildflowers if the views aren’t clear.

Definitely longer than 16km, my Fitbit calculated 22kms. Beautiful scenery and lookouts, one of the best hikes in Ontario. Challenging climbs and descents throughout, pay attention to the trail markers and be prepared for 7hour hike. Bring water & snacks. Flashlight (not cell phone) helped us because we didn’t make it out before dark. Went near the end of fall, leaves covered the rocks adding to the challenge.  Definitely moderate ++ trail.

Beautiful views from the cliffs. Took around 5 hours and totaled 11 miles. The rocks that make up most of the trail can become very slippery especially after it rains, so be careful. Definitely one for the memory books.

very reasonable challenge level (for a novice hiker!). rocks did get slippery after some light rain that morning, but nothing that hiking shoes can't handle. stunning views and wasn't too busy over thanksgiving weekend, although we did head out somewhat earlier around 9am.
Was a rainy morning though the trail was still great, finished in 7 hours with a lunch and tea breaks.
Amazing trail. Took quite a bit longer than 4 hours.
Definitely watch for the poison ivy but overall a great hike!
Great trail, challenging with lots of elevation change and amazing views.

Best hike I've done in Ontario so far. 18-20 km for sure. Rugged terrain, lots of ups and  downs- inclines, declines, cliffs and mossy rocks were a bit slippery. Pay attention to marking on trees to stay on track lol. If the ground feels extra soft... take a better look at where your headed. Bugs were annoying at the end but it is what it is. Beautiful views, very entertaining, not a lot of people. Get the full day parking that way you don't have to worry.

Beautiful scenery and terrain :)
I want to warn people that it is definitely longer than 16km. My phone tracked at 20.7km.
Easy. Literally a baby could do it without any milk
Awesome. Only the distance is almost 2km longer then posted on all tails app
A bit tricky in a few spots. Gorgeous views. Enjoyed walking it counterclockwise to see good AM light on the east side and PM on the West.

Need hiking shoes with good solid soles. Lots of walking on rocks and roots. Beautiful hike with spectacular views.
In

Great trail, pretty rock and some steep rock areas towards the shore cliff sections so wouldn't recommend that side of the trail for bringing any older/small dogs. 

Definitely bring them leashed as there's around a dozen spots you'll be walking right beside the cliff edge
Very well marked trail, easy to navigate. Big inclines, considerate elevation gain by Ontario standards. Main attraction is Lion’s lookout.
Great trail ! Nice challenge
Love it.
lots of nice lookouts. the starting section is private so we had to detour (although we did the trail in reverse, so that may have been why)

Started at the Cemetery Rd. Entrance (free parking), did the full loop. Approximately 17km. Last half was very rocky with steep ￼inclines. Bring walking poles because the trail is very hard on knees. The views were amazing!
Lots of poison ivy, be careful! Parked at the arena for $15/day, easy walk to the trail head.
The trail was great, it took us longer than expected to get to the lookout so we cut back through an old trail and it was perfect
A full day jaunt for me and my wife ; we both agreed this was our favourite trail in Ontario. A bit less crowded then the national park but with all of the same views. A great hike
very nice
Longer than expected with wet rocks. More people than expected between McCready and the Lookout.
I did a part of this hike in October 2021. the view ontop was amazing
Took us way longer than we thought, but the views were amazing! Lots of rocks, tree roots, and ups and downs. Wear good hiking shoes and bring your poles.
Best trail experience I have ever head + fabulous view

Nice trail with beautiful views!
BEWARE OF PARKING! 4 hours is not enough to comfortably finish the entire big loop. I had to run back to my car at the end and almost fainted
Beautiful hiking. Scenic views. Strongly recommended
Rocky for the first half, be watchful for trail markers, with fallen tree and other obstacles it's easy to miss them

Trail is great. 
Has anyone that has used the campsites on the trail no where a good spot to overnight park is?

My fastest time for the 16.5 km route from the normal parking lot is 1 hour and 42 minutes.  no water.  no shirt.  only shoes, shorts, 60 calories, no socks but a heart rate monitor.  I had done the loop about 8 times.  sometimes carry a pack that weighed over 40lbs just to see.  that time was just over 2 hours.  maybe 2 hours 15.

Really great trail. 

If you are going to do the whole loop in the winter time snow shoes are a must.
Great winter hike!!

Wonderful trail with fantastic views at the lookouts. After Thanksgiving is the perfect time to go with cool weather and without bugs or people - we didn't see a single person past the parking lot. Trail was well marked with maps at intersections. Most of the trail involves watching your step so the uneven terrain (plus rain) made this take closer to 6 hours. Would still rate it as moderate but be prepared for a long one.
Excellent trail

Wonderful trail, very scenic and interesting. I hiked with my 14 yr old son who’s been hiking with me since he was 2. We found the trail about moderate. Some say it’s hard, but bring your kids, they are capable of more then you might think, and might enjoy it very much. Just be careful of the cliffs! 

We only wore basic hiking shoes, brought one small backpack with some water and snacks in it. If hiking with a teenage boy, bring more snacks!
Amazing trail! Challenging but worth it. It's more like 20km.
Excellent!
It's normally a great trail, but now they have reserved parking that costs $35 for the day and bylaw enforcement offers on site. Rip off for the locals!

Beautiful views and lots to see. However, trail markings are at times a little hard to find and the path gets very close to the edge of the cliffs so be careful! Lots of walking on rocks and uneven ground so polls were nice to have with us. Overall a great trail and we will definitely be back.

We did the entire 18km Loop starting out at Cemetery Rd. There's a side trail here that connects with the Main trail bypassing the entire  McCurdy Parking lot. It's about 3.9KM. 

The trail was great, well Marked if you pay attention but challenging at times. I wouldn't recommend trying the full loop if you're not atleast a moderate to experienced Hiker or aren't used to hiking. Th entire loop took us 5 hours with two 30 minute breaks and that last 4KM was absolutely Grueling for us!! but this was our first time attempting a Hike longer then 12km. 

Bring Good shoes and lots of water if you atrempt the full loop. Good hiking shoes are a MUST. Leave plenty of time, we started out at 7:30am and finished just after 1:30PM. we kept a fast pace throughout the whole thing and took two 30 minute breaks along the way.

Lots of rocks and navigating the elevations. Saw very few hikers along the lookout trails to Lion’s Head Point. Lots of traffic from Lion’s Head Lookout heading toward the town, then nobody to the Cemetery Road parking.
I recommend doing the entire loop for the full Lion’s Head experience if you want a challenge. We took it slow, checking out the features and lookouts along the way. We even stopped at a rock beach to have our lunch. A great day!
Definitely a challenge. Fitbit says 112 flights of stairs. some waist high rocks to climb.  overall great views with a nice beach to stop for lunch and swim.
We started at the McCurdy Drive Parkette and did the main loop. According to my Fitbit, It was 20km (definitely not 15k). There are lots of pretty lookouts, so plan 5 hours minimum with some stops.

Definitely more of a 17 km hike so be sure to wear the right shoes because blisters are a high possibility. We parked at the Cemetery Road Side Trail (free) so our trek was a bit different from the navigation. 
The hike was worth it just for that view. Beautiful.
Some trails are closed so it’s more like a 17km hike and you only get a 4 hour parking limit. But other that that is was amazing!
Long hike without the side trail
It was a long one !!
The trail is lovely but has lots of rocks and roots so hiking shoes are a must. Great views and gorgeous cliffs

We did the same as another reviewer, leaving from cemetery road (free, empty) parking in the morning and going counterclockwise. All together the hike was an enjoyable 15.5 km (4 hrs moving time). Agree with others that good shoes are needed. Also trail out to the shore from the parking lot is *full* of poison ivy which is hard not to walk through, so take precautions. We also lunched at the shore. A really beautiful day for a hike

We did our hike on a Wednesday morning and got started at 7:30 am. We decided to park at the end of Cemetery Rd where it is free. There is enough room for about 8 cars. The hike took us 5.5 hours, we did it counterclockwise, with a stop for a bite to eat at the rocky beach close to Mackay Harbour. The total distance was 15.7 km. Good footwear is a must as portions of the trail are rocky with many raised tree roots, which can be slippery. There are parts which require some scrambling, but not too difficult. The bugs weren’t bad on that day, but I can see them being a problem in the forested parts away from the water. Bring plenty of water, we had 3 litres for the two of us, and snacks for nourishment. The scenery was beautiful and the portion hiked to get to the lookout wasn’t busy at all. We encountered 3 people. Great hike!
Warning! if paying for parking it takes about 1 hour to get to first lookout. With Moore St. Trailhead closed it takes a lot longer. Ps. Very muddy and slippery. $60 parking ticket

Great views but the hike was more challenging than I expected, the hike itself was about 17km that took about 4.5 hours . Went counterclockwise and took the Donna Baker and Inland side trails to get to the lookout (due to running out of time). Definitely take bug spray, water, and energy bars if you’re planning to do the full loop. Also give yourself plenty of time, got lost a couple of times and had to jog parts of the trail to make it back to the bus.
Nice long hike along the coast. It took us 6 hours. Recommend it!
Amazing trail..  took over 6’ hours for the full trail, with the closed section it’s almost 17km.  So worth it!!

3.5 if I could give it that but I can’t. The trail was good, definitely fits the moderate rating it was given. There is elevation gain and some rough terrain which I love in a hike. The view is okay. Granted, we came when it was grey and a thunderstorm came down about 3 hours into our hike but the view itself was pretty underwhelming.

incredible , rough terrain in many side trails and main trail areas, bring good shoes lots of water. be watchful with the side trials I got a little lost but its because I am a beginner. was there for 8 to 9 hours, beautiful fantastic hike, absolutely unforgettable
Spectacular views. Rugged terrain not for beginners. Bring lots of water food & bug spray. Good shoes a must. Glad we did it. Took 7.5 hours; 17.5km. Check this off the bucket list.

Views were spectacular, path was tricky in some areas and easy in others, markings were easy to see, definitely bring lots of water, good footwear recommended, some free parking at end of Cemetery Road, and we will definitely do this hike again. Note that the Bruce Trail Moore Street Side Trail was recently closed by the Bruce Trail Conservancy, at the request of the landowners, due to trail degradation and environmental damage. Access to the Lion's Head Lookout is only available from the main trail entrance at the McCurdy parking lot or at the end of Cemetery Road (and currently numbers aren't monitored even though the trail is generally at over capacity during good weather days). The McCurdy parking lot is a small parking lot, with 4 porte-potties and trash/recycle bins, but no other facilities. Overflow parking is available at the Lion's Head Arena (near the LCBO on Ferndale Road) and just walk the 1 km back to the McCurdy main trail entrance. As of August 2020, no parking is permitted on Moore St. (from hospital to the end of the road). In addition, if you are using Google/GPS to get to this destination, the directions that take you to the end of Moore St. with access to the Lookout are INCORRECT. This is a residential area and all property is private, therefore no trespassing - use the main trail. Littering and trail degradation is a real problem in this Nature Preserve - so please do your part - even consider finding another trail in the area to reduce the over-use.

Things you need to know:
This trail is absolutely stunning. 5/5 on the views. They are unreal. The loop is not 15km, it is closer to 18 according to my tracking app. But it is not a “walk in the part 18km,”, it is a “trek through the rocks and boulders 18km” which will make you tired AF. It is proper moderate which means it leans more toward difficult than easy. As others have said before, you should start with the lookouts, then do the rest of it (go clockwise) because you will be too tired/sore by the end of it to enjoy the views. We are experienced hikers and do one or two 10km+ hikes every week and our feet hurt, our ankles were sore and we were just overall exhausted by the end. You pretty much have to watch your step all the way until the last few kms. 
There are portapotties at the parking lot. They were gloriously clean when we went, so we really enjoyed that. Otherwise throughout the entire trail you’re on your own, so bring a dog bag for your TP if you use it.
BRING A TON OF WATER. We were two adults and a dog and we brought almost 5 liters… drank it all, could have used more, honestly. It was hot and the constant rocks and climbing do make you sweat quite a bit.
There were no bugs at all (July 25, 2020). We went in the morning, around 9 am and finished by 4pm ish. We took our time with photos, had breakfast at one of the lookouts. It was gorgeous. Then we had lunch later on in the hike. Bring a bathing suit because there is a beautiful beach so if you feel like peeling your hiking attire off, there is the most pristine clear water waiting for you. That was the only part that had a few bugs though. FYI.
The parking lot was almost empty when we started but by the time we ended, the street had cars lined up for about a km so I recommend going up early as the short look is very popular so tons of people come to hike it. 
There are three hikes within this trail, the full one (this one), the inland loop (slightly shorter) and just over to the lookouts (fairly short). NONE OF THEM would be comfortable in flip flops. You will do yourself a favour by wearing proper shoes. When we were coming back we saw a bunch of people in flop flops. This is not flip flop kind of a walk. The rocks are slippery and they are everywhere and some are BIG… not flip flop kind of a hike.

We did this trail Summer 2019, it was crowded as in we probably passed 5-6 families. Plenty to see in this trail; many lookouts, rocks to climb over, clearing with water to cross and fields of tall trees. It was beautiful!
great hike with plenty of amazing views and look outs!

Great trail, very challenging winter hike. Snow shoes, micro spikes and gaiters are a must. Few steep sections where my snow shoes were not enough. The end and beginning of the trail is well marked but be prepared to trail blaze on your own in the mid section with little guidance from the blazes (especially since they’re white and very spread out). Lots of trees blown down over the trail make for great scrambling opportunities. Did this hike solo with a couple stops and took about 5 hours total in the snow.
Incredible hike. Plan ahead with food, water, and keep an eye on the blazes. It's possible to get off course in the rocky sections near the cliffs.

The best hike I’ve been on this year! Nonstop breathtaking vistas of  Georgian Bay! Mistimed the return a little, and had to get rescued in the middle of the woods in the middle of the night. 5 stars for the rescue crew, super prompt and siccc ATV skills. Highly recommend!

Definitely one of very best sections!  Breathtaking views, vegetation varies throughout, and tricky rock sections.  So worth it!  Have done this trail early Spring 2016  and also early Fall 2018.   Ensure you have your map app downloaded and pay attention.
Great
Pretty view when you get to the water.

If you like to walk on the edge of a cliff this is your trail !
Wonderful views of you don't fear heights

I'd highly recommend this trail. The hike to the cliffside is roughly 30-45 minutes and it's well worth it. Stunning views of the turquoise water of Isthmus Bay and Lion's Head Harbour is a sight to see.

As for the quality of the trail, I would bring shoes with a lot of grip, as it get's quite rocky once you get closer to the lookout. Also, there's no railings at the top, so watch your footing close to the edge.
easy hike with little elevation. beautiful view once you get to the water. there's a bit of a walk in the forest before the ascent.

One of the best hikes I have done this year! Loved the various different landscapes, rocky, sandy, grassy, forest, waterfront. Phenomenal lookouts. Started from the Moore St. Access point. First half from this point is easy, second half gets more strenuous. Finished in under 6 hours with many stops for views and a short lunch. Very rewarding.

This was a lovely trail with many gorgeous views. Concur with most reviews here, a few spots to get mixed up in, trail under water at beach... follow the shoreline and watch for markers. Took about 5 hours from Moore St. to Cemetery Road. Lots of ups and downs and very rocky, suggest ankle support. There are also moderate amounts of poison ivy to watch for between the lions head section and the beach, coming along the trail at on the barrels bay side and then some dense patches coming out to cemetery road. Be vigilant in keeping an eye out for it as you won’t see any then all of sudden you see a bit. 
Had a great day, club and park do a great job here.

We did the full loop in just over 6 hours with a stop for lunch and many photo opportunities. We were with my in-laws in their 50s so could likely do it faster depending on your speed and fitness level while still enjoying breaks. 

The first half of the the hike was beautiful with many stunning lookouts over turquoise water and cliffs. It then descends down to a section on a rocky beach. I had the impression this section extended further into the second half of the hike which would have allowed for more opportunity to swim, however the second half was more of a forest hike. The final 5km is a forest trail and easier terrain mainly flat. If I were doing it again I would hike to the water and turn back vs. completing the full loop. As others mentioned do make sure to have lots of water. We did it in running shoes and it was fine but ideally would have preferred to have my hiking shoes for this one as quite rocky and lots of roots.
Great hike into and out of the lookout points! Took the Moore Street side trail in as time was a factor. Incredible views!
I love this trail. beautiful views and properly marked signs
great views, and a lovely rock beach to swim at part way through. took 6.5 hrs with lots of stops for pictures.

We hiked in from the Moore Side Street Trail and proceeded to follow the white Bruce Trail Markets walking in a clockwise direction. The views get spectacular as you walk along the bluff. Best to have proper hiking boots as terrain is quite rocky and rugged, not a flat path. Lots of up 2-3 metres, then down 2-3 metres. If you get the jitters walking close to the edge of the bluff, beware. Lots of close to the edge of the bluff walking, but the views are amazing. We “cut our hike short” and returned via the Inland Side Trail, instead of completing the full loop. Cuts about 3 km off the hike. The Inland Side Trail follows blue markers and is much less travelled, yet easily followable as a trail. No views here. Just a lumpy walk through the forest to get you back to the main Bruce Trail close to the Lion’s Head Lookout. 
Caution ... bring twice the water you normally bring as there is nothing en route. You can drink out of the Bay if needed with no real concerns. 
Bottom Line ... A spectacular hike. We completed 13.0 km in 5 hours with stops to enjoy the view and a longer stop for lunch. Plan accordingly. Don’t get caught after dark. It will be a very unpleasant night if you are not prepared. Enjoy!!!

Took 2 cars and parked at the Moore st lot and Cementary rd lot. Hiked clockwise from Moore lot to the Cemetery lot and the approx 13km hike took our group 5  hours including a stop for lunch at the rock beach. Trail was pretty well marked and easy to follow most of the time except along the rock beach where the trail follows the beach which is under water for a small section. We had to do a little bush wacking to reconnect with the trail but it was a fairly short detour. Views from the top are spectacular and we even got to watch some rock climbers.
Do friendly but rocky!! Went out a bit and came back! Was a good hike!

This trail is a lot of fun  and requires lots of energy and time to complete!  Most of it is well marked but it does get a little weird after the white rocky beach.   You really have to follow the water’s edge to find the next trail blazer.  We stopped a number of times for the views and we also got a little lost near the end and had to backtrack a bit.   That was simply due to fatigue and not paying attention.  You really need to keep watching for the blazers :)

We found a good spot to park on Moore street near the Yacht club, ample parking, this took us about 7.5km to hike to the lions head! We hiked through the rain and it was the most amazing hike I’ve been on to this day. Mostly all uphill on stepping stones, careful of tree roots and little potholes! Just absolutely amazing at every look out!  Would’ve tried the whole 15km had it not been raining so hard.
Very rocky - to the point where ankles/knees hurt. By far the nicest part are the first 2-3 miles (clockwise).

Great trail - if i do it again, i will start through Finnigans forest. I clocked 9.8 miles in less than 4 hours. Either start the trail at an appropriate hour or bring appropriate head gear. Trail is moderate with trail conditions, easy elevation!

There is a beach section where the trail markers are below the tide line. The map here is correct, stick close to the water and you'll find the next marker.

We were in a rush due to sundown and got the whole loop done in under 4 hrs.

If you only want to walk a shorter distance or walk along the cliffs and enjoy the view, you should start the way up at Lion’s Head and not at the cemetery street - there you first have to walk through the forest for several kilometers. 
The views over Lions Head and the lake are fantastic. There are three marked lookouts on the map.

Not sure what happened but after we saw the two outlooks all the markers to take us around the loop were no longer there...we weren’t the only ones who had to turn back because the markers could not be found. We then took another trail that was led by another set of white blazers and that too just abruptly ended. Just wasn’t our day, I guess.

Decided to try this trail due to the moderate rating a while ago during fall. It was quite interesting...as we got STUCK in the dark and had to get rescue out!! We needed an extra hour to get out and it happened to be day lights savings so we lost that hour. So...that being said this trail was stunning but it was DIFFICULT. It will take longer than expected at least in the fall and winter where the ground is more covered. Lots of big and small Rocks to climb and step through. Changes pretty frequently in elevations once you pass the dirt road at the beginning. Start early in the morning or do not go...this took us 7ish hours but I'd say add an extra hour if you plan to stop often for the beautiful views. I'd still say it was worth it for us in the end though, I'd have to say this area has a great search and rescue
one of the best.

Spectacular hike of Lions Loop Trail today. Beautiful lookouts with nearly 10 km of coastline. No bugs thanks to cooler temps. Completed trail in 5.5 hours with 2 nutrition breaks and took in all of the lookouts plus bonus of a moose! Highly recommend this hike.

Did the horseshoe shape trail about 5-1/2 hours. Stopped for lunch and lots of lookouts. No bugs beautiful day few hikers few climbers take water and sturdy shoes. Something different around every turn. Enjoyed it very much

We did the trail at a moderate pace and stopped at just about every opportunity for a lookout (there’s lots!) and at the beach. It took us 6.5 hours to complete the whole loop. Very rocky and with recent rains it was a little slippery. Bring good footwear. A lot of up and down on rocks but not extremely challenging- a fun day hike.

We did the entire trail and it is difficult for people who are active and in good shape! It’s not worth walking the entire trail because all the views are the same. 
Bring water and don’t start too late because you may get stuck in the trail and not be able to find the markers to get out.

Absolutely stunning hike. Be sure to bring plenty of water and wear supportive shoes as you'll be walking on boulders, trails, roots, etc. Dunking our heads in the Bay was a lifesaver when we were getting so hot.

Amazing trail with stunning lookouts. Hiked it with our two dogs.
Bring lots of water and wear comfortable footwear as it’s up and down most of the way.

Well marked very pretty
Felt safe 
Plenty look outs

Great hike with signs all the way along. It took us 4,5 hours with a good pace. For sure the terrain is good for kids too. There is loads of wonderful views and to our surprise it was great for walk even in mid of October!

Great trail. Took us 5.5 hours. Could have done it quicker but you have to take advantage of the lookout views in the fall. We were fortunate the weather was unusually warm in the middle of October. Even took a dip in the c-c-c-cold Georgian Bay. Well worth it

Great trail. Great views of Georgain bay. The trail is well marked in most places. 
We hike the full loop, it took us 4.5 hrs. We moved at a good pace but I wouldn't say we were speeding through. We briefly stopped at the lookout and continued on.

Thanksgiving weekend w Bernie. Rained first hour, foggy and cloudy after that. Really beautiful hike, especially around lion’s head look off, worth doing again in sunny weather. Trail was really rough!! Rocks and roots everywhere, made much harder by wet rocks. Not a difficult hike, no cardio minutes.

Beautiful scenery, there are different types of forests and a quiet atmosphere. Trail is very well labeled and accessible, don't have to worry about getting lost. If you are quiet enough you can see some animals.

We completed the entire loop in 6 1/2 hours and this was hauling a** with only short breaks along the way. Bring your bathing suit to so can go for a dip once you reach the rock beach. The trail is not overly difficult but lots of elevation change. We found the rocks to be very slippery. Bring lots of water, we only brought 2 bottles each and could of used 4 each. it was definitely a work out and we were very exhausted by the end but it was worth it.

This is a fantastic hike but it is quite challenging. My wife and I did the entire loop and thoroughly enjoyed the scenic views all along the way. However, it took us 6 hours, we also had a 2-1/2 year old on our backs practically the whole time. He only ended up walking maybe 2km out of the entire 17km trail. We’re pretty avid hikers and we both work out several times a week. Both of us were quite sore after this trail as it is fairly rugged. If you’re going to hike the entire loop be prepared for a long day and bring plenty of water and food.
Really good trail and the view of the cliff was beautiful!!!
Beautiful trail. The view over the cliffs is breathtaking.

Bonded and happy until kilometre 10. 
Definitely bring snacks and water ! Keep your sanity strong out there folks. 
7 hours for 15km ... with breaks
Great look out points! 16kms of moderate terrain. lots of little up and down hills. Great for adults but the whole trail maybe a little tough for kids.
Awesome trail. Stunning view into Georgian Bay. The overnight rest area is spacious and right in the water. Highly recommend it!
Four hours and thirty minutes total. Stopped for lunch and again for a swim. Dog friendly.
Was the highlight of our week long trip! Our 8-11 year old girls finished it and had a blast. Amazing views, some difficult terrain. Now my wife and I want to trek the entire Bruce trail.

If you end up staying over at the harbour, be sure you DO have a propane burner or such as the wood in the area is usually very damp and many larger pieces of wood are gone later in the summer months. Overall a beautiful hike with some moderately challenging elevations (closer to the lake side)

Highly recommended
Fantastic hike. Elevation will make it take longer so start early. Great swimming spot half way in.
Really good trail. Make sure you pack plenty of water and snacks with lots of energy. Did the whole thing along with most of the side trials.

This trail has amazing views. Definitely bring snacks and lots of water! We didn’t do the full 15km loop. There are lots of opportunities via side trails to make this hike shorter if necessary. This trail is pretty rugged, but very enjoyable. Due to the steep cliffs and crevices, it’s probably not a great idea to bring kids. I will definitely be doing this hike again!
Beautiful vistas. We did the full 15+km loop. I’d definitely wear hiking shoes/boots. My runners didn’t cut it.
Best Trail ! Beautiful View ! Easy and breathtaking!
The lookout point is absolutely breathtaking. So worth the trek!
awesome trail! light house should not be missed!

Absolutely amazing. It is a very difficult trail, though. It seems it's designed to break your ankles, lol. The air pressure(?) changes when you get up onto the cliff, and it feels like a different world. McKay Harbor is an overnight camping spot (no fires allowed, AMAZING spot though), and from the Harbor down to Cemetery road (bottom right corner) might be the hardest spot. Definitely recommend a sandwich and some granola bars (I found eating a clif bar on the cliff somewhat humorous) and taking LOTS of water. Highly recommend a camelbak. <3 <3 <3

very NICE trail To do
and not to hard when rail is dry.

Not 15 km. Got lost. Did 27.... my bad.  Even going the wrong way for 3km is worth it if there's a view right?  Highly recommend bringing snacks to avoid that high noon hangry faze, small pack of carrots IS NOT ENOUGH.  I repeat, snacks are a must!!  Brought two dogs with me, one was really handy pulling me up the inclines during the hangry/crying phase of our adventure.  The other was nothing more than a cute 20lbs  sack of potatoes I had to carry the whole time.  Ladies, put that long hair in a bun cause the spiders are cray cray up in there.  Went for a swim and found that 5 had caught a free ride!   I can not stress enough that is was not 15km, I wish knew that so I could have brought a tent... or some more snacks!
Amazing views! Long hike.
Awesome hike, great views, all kinds of terrain.
Just beautiful.
Nice hike and great view.  Would say 75% of the trail is moderate the rest is a little harder. Go early and bring a snack - it's a long haul.
did the 15km, no regrets
Great hiking! Definitely want to come back in the fall!
Love the rough terrain and the elevation that gives you the best look outs but you have to be really cautious if you are going in spring as snow makes it way more difficult and dangerous

An amazing trail with stunning views. Trails are well maintained. A lot of elevation changes. Bring water and snacks for sure as well as proper footwear. If planning on doing the whole loop leave early as to finish with some day light.
Amazing trail ... very rough terrain.  Make sure to leave enough time to complete the loop in the daylight.
Very beautiful hard hike, rough terrain but the look out points are well worth it!! Breathtaking
Beautiful hike and great view of Georgian Bay. I've hiked in a lot of places and didn't expect the moderating of this hike. Definitely a fun one and very scenic.
Great views!

It was a gorgeous day. Couldnt have asked for a better day. Aside from scaling the side of a cliff, I'd hate to see a "hard" trail from those rating this as moderate... I'd say that my family is quite fit and this trail proved to be a hard one. A lot of trecherous paths, roots, and rocks. The scenery was absolutely stunning and well worth the 5 hour drive for us. Because it was such a long drive we were only able to hike a small portion of the trail and we were out on it for 6 hours. Definitely would go back and finish it.

If you like beautiful Georgian bay this trail is for you. Although it's rated as moderate, l found this trail extremely tough on my almost 60 year old body. lt"s an very rugged trail full of rocks , roots and very hilly. You're constantly up and down. Follows the lake on a good part of the trail with a ton of beautiful scenic views. Took me 6 hrs to travel the 10 miles; my fitness counter counted 31, 800 steps and 28 km. Thoroughly enjoyed it and will tackle it again this fall when the leaves change. If you have any problems with your knees this is definitely not for you. I also wouldn't recommend doing this hike in the rain, you're navigating over stone most of the trail and it would be quite slippery. You don't want to fall on this trail.

Very nice moderate trail, beautiful, well marked. Perfectly challenging and rewarding for my first hiking adventure! Had a Lifestraw but water sources are not readily available..would definitely carry more next time. also water shoes if you plan on going in the lake.

An excellent day hike taking 6-7 hours to complete due to the challenging footing on the trail. Side trails can be used to shorten trail distance. Note that few sections of the trail are flat earth. Most involve walking over and around limestone rocks. Elevation is easy/moderate. None of the cliff lookouts have guardrails. The trail is very well marked. During the summer, the trail see more activity from climbers than hikers and they only use the portion from Moore Rd. to Lion's Head itself. As of June 2017, a short portion of the trail along the lake shore is flooded due to high lake levels requiring going barefoot over some painful rocks. Water shoes or trail runners that can get wet are recommended.
Amazing views!! Great trail markings! Challenging footing! Not an easy trail but an unique experience! Good hiking boots it's a must !
Wonderful views challenging footing lots of options with side trails. Pot holes near Lions Head very interesting.
Beautiful trail and views, loved the blue water of Georgian Bay.
Beautiful view! If your not a fan of heights it may not be your cup of tea.

Have done this trail every September for
The past 3
Years and it is a great challenge and breathtaking terrain
Very challenging!! Awesome views and beautiful forests.
Great difficulties, awesome views, easy to get there and the trails are well indicated. All that without altering the natural look of the park. A must do.
